newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-European stocks fall, Greenspan jitters grow.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-European stocks fall, Greenspan jitters grow.

text.p: Most European stock markets fell on Monday as Wall Street again cashed in on last week's record run and investors started worrying about what U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan will say this week.
Paris suffered an extra headache with the announcement of big company tax rises aimed at cutting the French budget deficit for European monetary union, although prices bounced back before the close.
But the major depressant was New York, where investors took profits on Monday morning for the second session running after the Dow's brief trip over 8,000 last week.
The Dow hit a low of 7,840 points and although it later bounced back it was still down about 10 points at 7,900 when European markets closed for the day.

London was one of the biggest casualties, with the FTSE-100 closing down 71.5 points or 1.47 percent at 4,805.7 -- a far cry from Friday morning when it came within two points of breaking 5,000 for the first time.

But dealers remained largely confident. "There is some profit-taking but it is not a panic," said the head of equity trading at a U.S. investment bank. "The trend is still holding up and I would expect it to resume some time soon."

Markets were, however, nervous about the Humphrey-Hawkins testimony on Tuesday when Greenspan will report to Congress on the state of the U.S. economy. Greenspan sent stock markets plunging around the world last December when he warned investors against irrational exuberance.

Since then the bull run has resumed with a vengeance and economists say there are few major clouds on the horizon for the U.S. economy. Since last year Greenspan has said he has no intention of trying to prick a stock market bubble with higher short-term interest rates.
The French market was down for much of the day despite news of the company tax hikes.

Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn announced the government would cut the deficit by 32 billion francs ($5.3 billion) with 22 billion in higher taxes on companies' profits and capital gains and 10 billion in spending cuts.

This followed an audit of state finances which estimated that the public deficit would be 3.5 to 3.7 percent of GDP this year, well above the 3.0 percent target for joining the single European currency.
The CAC-40 index fell about 1.5 percent but rebounded to close down only 2.57 points (0.09 percent) at 2,874.12 as most of what Strauss-Kahn said had been leaked.
"The impact on the markets was mitigated because 80 percent of what was announced today was known," said economist Jean-Louis Mourier at Louis Dreyfus Finance.

Frankfurt had a volatile day with the IBIS index of electronic trade jumping around 1.7 percent to a high of 4,211 on news that two of Germany's largest commercial banks, Bayerische Vereinsbank AG and Bayerische Hypobank, would merge.
Later it fell as the profit-taking malaise reached Germany before bouncing back to close up 8.02 points at 4,139.96. Hopes of further consolidation in the banking sector helped to support the market.

Floor trade was disrupted by computer problems but in the end the DAX index closed down 88.13 points or 2.1 percent at 4,108.40. This was more than London in percentage terms but the DAX closed on Friday before Wall Street tumbled and the index was therefore starting from a higher base than its electronic trading counterpart.
The dollar ended the European day on a firm note at 1.7953 marks and 115.85 yen, compared with 1.7892 and 115.35 in late trading on Friday.

The French budget audit pressured the mark as the market again contemplated the prospect of a large number of countries launching a weak euro in 1999. The mark fell to 3.3756 French francs and 972.75 Italian lire from Friday's closing levels of 3.3805 and 973.15.
CURRENCIES AT EUROPEAN CLOSE
The dollar was at 1.7952 marks and 115.70 yen, compared with 1.7892 and 115.35 in late trading on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS AT CLOSE
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index closed down 71.5 points or 1.47 percent at 4,805.7.
FRANKFURT - The IBIS index of electronic trade closed up 8.02 points at 4,139.96. The DAX index of floor trade closed down 88.13 points or 2.1 percent at 4,108.40.
PARIS - The CAC-40 closed down 2.57 points (0.09 percent) at 2,874.12.
PRECIOUS METALS AT CLOSE
Gold was at $326.95 after closing at $324.15 an ounce on Friday. Silver was down two cents at $4.28. ($ = 6.041 French Francs)
